newsitem.title: USA: Box of tarantulas may settle Chicago law suit.
newsitem.headline: Box of tarantulas may settle Chicago law suit.

text.p: A Chicago businessman said he may have to settle a legal dispute with a former partner by sending him a box of tarantulas.
"I would think it may come to that. I don't have anything in the bank," said Bryant Capiz, president of Arachnocentric, a mail-order company based here that sells exotic spiders.
Capiz, who calls himself 'The Spiderman,' is fascinated by arachnids and started the business six years ago as a hobby. "It was always in my blood," he said.
He later went into partnership with a friend, Raul Aldape, but the two had a falling out. This week Aldape sued Capiz to get back his investment in the business.
Aldape and his attorney could not be reached for comment.

Capiz said Aldape wants $40,000 but may have to settle for a portion of the inventory in the company's small store. About 2,000 spiders share shelf space at Arachnocentric with unusual snakes, lizards and pet supplies, Capiz said.

One of the store's most popular items is the Goliath Bird-eater, a spider the size of a dinner plate that sells for up to $100 and eats crickets and mice. "It's a macho thing. The guys want them," Capiz said.
Baby spiders are bred in the store and account for a large portion of sales, said Capiz, an expert in spider breeding.
Although the business is struggling, he said he finds it satisfying. "At least I get to do what I love every day."
